To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the physical modeling of motion and dispersion of different density gas pollutant plumes by means of wind tunnel experiments is possible only if the Froude numbers are the same for the model and the real object, and if the Froud number for the model is greater than one, which is a very rare case in practice.
the physical experiments in low speed wind tunnels cannot be used for modeling the plumes of different densities gas pollutants.

it is not possible to model the motion and dispersion of different density gas polluting plumes in wind tunnel physical experiments based on physical similarity, because the Froude similarity criterion is not valid in the case of gas pollutants of different density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the influence of the model scale and the Froude criterion on the dispersion of gas pollutants in the atmosphere.
the analysis of the influence of the air flow velocity, the gas pollutant density ratio and the model scale on the Froude similarity criterion.
the analysis of the applicability of the Froude criterion for modeling motion and dispersion of different density gas plumes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Froude criterion is not sufficient for modeling motion and dispersion of different density gas pollutant plumes in wind tunnels.
it is possible to model motion and spreading of gas pollutant plumes of different densities in lowspeed wind tunnel experiments based on the Froude criterion, however with some limitations.
it is not possible to model the motion and dispersion of gas pollutants with a density different from the air in low-speed wind tunnels based on physical similarity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wind tunnel experiments can model the dispersion of a gas pollutant with a density up to 1.5 times higher compared to air, if the model scale does not exceed 0.3 m.
the wind tunnel physical experiments can only be used to model the motion of plumes of gas pollutants of similar density to the air.
the physical experiments in low-speed wind tunnels are suitable to model the motion and dispersion of low-density pollutants, but not suitable for high-density pollutants.
The main takeaway from our work is that

physical experiments in wind tunnels can be used to obtain qualitative data on gas plumes of different densities, but the results cannot be used to obtain quantitative information on the dispersion process in real conditions.

the Froude criterion does not allow to model the real phenomena with the same density of the air and gas pollutants, which is the case in reality, but only with a density of the air flow and the gas pollutant, which is the same.
the Froude criterion can be used for the modeling of motion and dispersion of different density gas plumes, but only in a limited range of the Froude numbers.
